families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

meaning: Each tie is a pointer that landed. Whether the paper and the Lean say the same thing is a reading.

rows.fidelity_note: The linked definition is the transpose action of a linear map on a vector. It contains no assertion about verification runs or a disagreement between two independently checked statements, so that historical claim needs its cited run evidence.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.transposeApply

rows.fidelity_note: The theorem gives the conjunction of whole-space and torus breakdown from the complete cell condition. Its premise does not assert that numerical data satisfying the condition have been supplied.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.spaceAndTorusBreakdown_of_cell_system_condition

rows.fidelity_note: The linked condition is the full fifteen-clause premise referred to in the implication. It specifies what the data must satisfy and contains no numerical witness.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The second clause requires exactly the seven stated properties: positive periods, positive constant weight, closure under negation and reflection, inclusion of zero, and coverage of the reference harmonics.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The third clause expands to the local elimination comparison, global form comparison, row and pressure identities, and exterior cover conditions. The detailed matrix and radius conditions are more explicit than the paper’s discussion, as the passage says.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The fourth clause requires the enclosure inequalities for the particular constants used in the final estimate, uniformly for all parameters in K. The earlier existence of some enclosure constants is a separate condition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: Substituting the fixed coercivity 3/50 and weight 39/50 in the fifth clause gives the first lower bound in (B.22). The multiplier constant includes the same weight and enclosure terms.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The sixth clause is c₂ ≥ √(1000/(3/50)) = √(1000·50/3), the second inequality of (B.22).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The eighth clause requires the profile, pressure and adjoint representations together, including joining and endpoint conditions. Its pressure identity uses the gradient of the represented pressure minus |Wᵃ|²/2, and selected adjoints have decay order at least three.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The ninth clause controls the constant, linear and quadratic coefficients inside the matching ball and the product of two exterior L² bounds. It retains the strict exterior condition |y|>rχ; replacing the sphere in the integral needs the stated null-set and integrability justification.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The tenth clause distinguishes the central gradient L² error from the parameter-dependent gradient L³ error and imposes their two different combinations for the gap and form shift.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The thirteenth clause identifies the adjoint and profile-direction data and requires the fitted-direction set to be empty. This removes the fitted terms from the general defect sum.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The field and reciprocal-period identities are imposed together with the empty fitted-direction set. Specialising the defect formula with these identities recovers the terms of (B.53).
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.AdjointEntryLinks

rows.fidelity_note: The fourteenth clause requires explicit valid potential series and compact pin generators, with identities tying them to the adjoint estimate. The paper gives their analytic consequences in (B.51) while omitting this coefficient format, so the passage correctly limits the comparison.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The linked condition requires resolved boundary degree at least one and agreement with the chosen volume and boundary degrees. The preliminary lower bound −1, the tested lower bound two and the axis restriction are imposed by the neighboring mesh and cell conditions described in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellModeLayouts

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSupportFacts
ties.plain: Forcing support lies in the cells

rows.fidelity_note: The support condition contains no nonnegative-radius requirement by itself. With no actuators and a negative chosen radius, its actuator clauses and square-cover clause can be vacuous; this says nothing about the remaining cell conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSupportFacts
rows.plain: Forcing support lies in the cells

rows.fidelity_note: The conditions impose parameter-uniform lower bounds on all five density coefficients, including a radius-squared weight on the velocity term, with coverage of unresolved modes. The paper explicitly leaves these full coefficient formulas unwritten.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The two branches give the zero-azimuthal and nonzero-azimuthal component formulas of (B.7) and (B.8). They are used to construct the divergence-free field once the shape and spline validity conditions hold.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedComps

rows.fidelity_note: The field conditions impose conjugation, reflection, the separate joining orders, vanishing at the origin and the required decay exponents. Compact support is imposed by the additional compact-field condition mentioned in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFieldData

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform
ties.plain: Fixed data across the parameter set

rows.fidelity_note: The reference model, harmonic bounds, mode classes, scalar weights and coercivity data are fixed throughout K. Only the rotation-frame entries are excluded from the fixed-weight identities, exactly as the passage specifies.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform
rows.plain: Fixed data across the parameter set

rows.fidelity_note: The target is required to equal the pin functional applied to the approximate-profile gradient for every parameter. Subtracting the same pin value therefore gives zero target gap.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.IsProfileShapeEntry

rows.fidelity_note: The local residual form is bounded above by retained potential plus retained pairing minus the top form plus the eliminated-band and eliminated-row terms. This is the stated ordering of the local comparison behind (B.26).
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationConditions

rows.fidelity_note: The admissible vector is fixed on used rows only up to complex gauge and pressure-head directions, and both actuator blocks must be real. This is the scope stated in the passage, which distinguishes it from simply substituting the paper’s global embedding.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange

ties.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellBlocks
ties.plain: Blocks and budgets for one cell

rows.fidelity_note: The linked data supply the scalar slack but do not define the eliminated-mode formula that divides by it. The division and its zero-slack safeguard are in the separate elimination formula and conditions.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellBlocks
rows.plain: Blocks and budgets for one cell

rows.fidelity_note: The potential conditions combine explicit decay powers with vanishing orders at the compactified endpoint. For the flux and pressure, the combined order must be at least two, agreeing with the mechanism described.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeries

rows.fidelity_note: This step combines the four analytic potential results into one common constant controlling both vector potentials, the flux and the pressure. Its analytic premises must be supplied by the preceding step named in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.PotentialShape.potentialData_of_series

rows.fidelity_note: The stated source gives continuously differentiable vector potentials, weak derivative identities for potentials, flux and pressure, and their pointwise or almost-everywhere decay bounds. It is the analytic conclusion identified in the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.IsPotentialData

rows.fidelity_note: The squared matrix norm is the sum of the squared Euclidean norms of its three columns, hence the squared Frobenius norm. Transposition preserves that sum.
rows.name: Breakdown.matSq

rows.fidelity_note: The divergence differentiates the matrix in each coordinate and applies it to the corresponding coordinate vector. With output coordinates in rows, this gives the transposed-flux divergence appearing in (B.52).
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.matrixDivergence

rows.fidelity_note: The current condition uses the reciprocal of (|m|+1/2)², which is smaller than the former reciprocal when m is nonzero, so its norm requirement is weaker. The linked definition alone cannot establish the historical change or the reported build status.
rows.name: Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded

rows.fidelity_note: The radius must be measurable, invariant under positive rescaling, and bounded everywhere between fixed positive lower and finite upper bounds. These are precisely the additional explicit requirements identified by the passage.
rows.name: Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionRadius

rows.fidelity_note: The complete condition provides fifteen exact targets for a checker-to-mathematics argument. The sentence asks for those targets to be justified and makes no claim that the numerical checks have already been supplied.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition

rows.fidelity_note: The linked condition states requirements on possible data and supplies neither a witness nor a contradiction. A statement about what an audit has demonstrated belongs to the audit record, rather than to this mathematical definition.
rows.name: Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCondition
